exposure: Clinical risk factors (pre-eclampsia, multiple pregnancy, assisted reproduction, antepartum bleeding, post-term delivery, obesity, episiotomy)
Haematological parameters (platelets, fibrinogen, APTT ratio, immature platelet fraction)
outcome: Immediate postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) defined as blood loss of at least 500 ml
cohort: The study included 2742 women who had a vaginal delivery between April 1, 2013 and May 29, 2015 in the maternity ward of Brest University Hospital, France.
finding: Besides classical clinical risk factors, simple haematological parameters such as platelets < 150 Giga/L, fibrinogen < 4.5 g/l, and APTT ratio >= 1.1 were identified as independent risk factors for immediate postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The study cohort exclusively included women who had a vaginal delivery, therefore findings are specific to this mode of birth.
